# `entity`

Generated by `entity-runtime-docs` from the clap definition in [`crates/entity-cli/src/cli.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/entity-runtime/blob/main/crates/entity-cli/src/cli.rs). It lists only commands that exist. `entity --version` prints the version, and `--help` after any command prints the text below.

```text
Schema-driven entity runtime: validate definitions, create instances, execute operations.

An entity type is a YAML document — schema, lifecycle, operations, preconditions, invariants,
events. The kernel decides `definition + instance + operation + arguments -> Decision`; this
command is the shell that reads the files and prints the decision.

Values passed with --fields, --instance and --arguments are read three ways:
  inline JSON        --fields '{"title": "Login fails"}'
  @<path>            --instance @ticket.json      (JSON or YAML)
  -                  --instance -                 (standard input; JSON or YAML)
Only one flag per invocation may read standard input. A Decision printed by `create` or `execute`
can be fed straight back as an --instance.

Exit codes: 0 decided · 1 refused (or a definition is invalid) · 2 invalid invocation.
```

## `entity validate`

Check definitions; report every file, and exit 1 if any is invalid

```text
Usage: entity validate <DEFINITIONS>...
```

| Argument | Required | Repeats | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `<DEFINITIONS>...` | yes | yes | none | Definition files, YAML. |

## `entity inspect`

Show what a definition declares: fields, states, rules, operations

```text

```

## `entity graph`

Draw a definition: its lifecycle, or the references between several definitions


## `entity create`

Create an instance: definition + id + fields -> Decision

```text
Usage: entity create [OPTIONS] --definition <DEFINITIONS> --id <ID>
```

| Argument | Required | Repeats | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--definition <DEFINITIONS>` | yes | yes | none | The definition file, YAML. Repeat to register several types or versions at once. |
| `--entity <ENTITY>` | no | no | none | Which type to create, when several `--definition` files were given. Several are needed whenever a definition declares a `ref`: the type it points at has to be registered too, or the registry is not a consistent set. With one file this is unnecessary and the type is unambiguous. |
| `--id <ID>` | yes | no | none | The new instance's identity. The kernel generates none; you supply it. |
| `--fields <FIELDS>` | no | no | `{}` | The fields, as inline JSON, `@<path>` or `-` for stdin. |
| `--store <STORE>` | no | no | none | A directory to keep the result in, so the next command can find it. Without one this prints a `Decision` and forgets it, which is the kernel's own shape: it decides and holds nothing. With one, the decision is committed — state and events together — and `execute --store` can pick the instance up by id instead of being handed it back on the command line. |
| `--record-id <RECORD_ID>` | no | no | none | Caller-supplied idempotency identity for this complete decision. |
| `--recorded-at <RECORDED_AT>` | no | no | none | When this was recorded, ISO-8601. Your clock: the kernel has none. |
| `--correlation <CORRELATION>` | no | no | none | The wider flow, when there is one. |
| `--causation <CAUSATION>` | no | no | none | What immediately led to this record, when there is one. |
| `--actor <ACTOR>` | no | no | none | Who asked. |
| `--no-actor` | no | no | none | Record explicitly that no actor caused this decision. |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | no | no | `json` | How to print the decision. One of `text`, `json`, `yaml`. |

## `entity execute`

Execute an operation: definition + instance + operation + arguments -> Decision

```text
Usage: entity execute [OPTIONS] --definition <DEFINITIONS> --operation <OPERATION>
```

| Argument | Required | Repeats | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--definition <DEFINITIONS>` | yes | yes | none | The definition file, YAML. Repeat to register several types or versions at once. |
| `--instance <INSTANCE>` | no | no | none | The current instance (or a Decision holding one), as inline JSON, `@<path>` or `-`. Not needed when `--store` and `--id` say where to find it, and refused beside them: two sources for one instance would leave the caller guessing which one decided. |
| `--store <STORE>` | no | no | none | A directory holding the instance, written by an earlier `create --store`. The instance is loaded from it, the decision is committed back to it at the revision that was loaded, and a concurrent writer is refused rather than overwritten. |
| `--id <ID>` | no | no | none | Which instance in the store to act on. |
| `--entity <WANTED_ENTITY>` | no | no | none | Which type to act on, when several `--definition` files were given. |
| `--operation <OPERATION>` | yes | no | none | The operation name, as declared in the definition. |
| `--arguments <ARGUMENTS>` | no | no | `{}` | The arguments, as inline JSON, `@<path>` or `-` for stdin. |
| `--expected-revision <EXPECTED_REVISION>` | no | no | none | The revision of the stored instance this request was decided on. Defaults to whatever the store holds when the command runs, which is what a sequential local command wants. Pass it when retrying: an already-accepted `--record-id` is returned as the original record only when the retry names the same revision the first request was decided on, so a lost response can be recovered after the subject moved. |
| `--record-id <RECORD_ID>` | no | no | none | Caller-supplied idempotency identity for this complete decision. |
| `--recorded-at <RECORDED_AT>` | no | no | none | When this was recorded, ISO-8601. Your clock: the kernel has none. |
| `--correlation <CORRELATION>` | no | no | none | The wider flow, when there is one. |
| `--causation <CAUSATION>` | no | no | none | What immediately led to this record, when there is one. |
| `--actor <ACTOR>` | no | no | none | Who asked. |
| `--no-actor` | no | no | none | Record explicitly that no actor caused this decision. |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | no | no | `json` | How to print the decision. One of `text`, `json`, `yaml`. |

## `entity list`

List what a store holds for one entity type: every identity, sorted, one per line. The question `create --store` and `execute --store` could not answer: they can act on an instance whose id you already know, and nothing could say which ids there are. A shell that did not write a store has to be able to ask it what it holds before it can do anything else.

```text
Usage: entity list [OPTIONS] --store <STORE> --entity <ENTITY>
```

| Argument | Required | Repeats | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--store <STORE>` | yes | no | none | The directory an earlier `create --store` wrote into. |
| `--entity <ENTITY>` | yes | no | none | Which entity type to list. |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | no | no | `text` | How to print the identities. One of `text`, `json`, `yaml`. |

## What an `eventlog-providers` build adds

The tables above describe the default build, which is what the release archives and a plain `cargo install` contain. Building `entity-cli` with the `eventlog-providers` Cargo feature (Rust 1.91) adds the items below, read from the `#[cfg(feature = "eventlog-providers")]` items of the same definition. `--help` on such a build prints their exact flags.

| Command | Adds | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `entity create` | `--eventlog-config <EVENTLOG_CONFIG>` | Eventlog File selection JSON; selects the recorded facade for `--store`. |
| `entity execute` | `--eventlog-config <EVENTLOG_CONFIG>` | Eventlog File selection JSON; selects the recorded facade for `--store`. |
| `entity list` | `--eventlog-config <EVENTLOG_CONFIG>` | Eventlog File selection JSON; selects the recorded facade for `--store`. |
| `entity store` | subcommand `entity store provision-eventlog-file` | Prepare a new recorded Eventlog File authority and print its exact reopen authority. |
